properties.decision: Chosen: owner rules on the result. A result that contradicts a prediction still CONTESTS it on its own (dec:idea-an-objection-resting-on-evidence-contests-or-refutes stands). The owner settles it with a signed ruling naming the result ("refuted by experiment E"); the claim then reads refuted BY THAT RULING, citing E, and conditional on the held model and the idealizations it rests on. Rejected: (b) a prediction stated before the data refutes itself automatically when a result contradicts it, conditional on the held model; (c) leave results only contesting.
properties.name: An experiment's result refutes a prediction only on the owner's signed ruling; on its own it contests
properties.rationale: Gap 1 of the design-a-phenomenon skill (#807): a result could only contest, never refute. Anthony's 10-20 rule says evidence alone contests and the owner settles it; (a) keeps that rule and gives the settling an act. It matches how physics works (Duhem-Quine): a failed prediction may be the hypothesis, the model, an idealization or the instrument, and the scientist judges which; the tool must not decide a falsification. (b) would narrow an accepted decision and let the tool make that judgement.
